stem.en: A rubbed balloon sticks to the wall, and the wall was never rubbed. Why?

text.en: The balloon's charge pulls the opposite charge in the wall a little closer and pushes the same charge a little further away, so the near side of the wall is opposite to the balloon and the two attract.

feedback.en: The wall has equal amounts of both kinds and no extra of either. A balloon that is not rubbed does not stick to it.

text.en: The balloon is sticky from Kabir's hair.

feedback.en: A balloon rubbed on a clean dry cloth sticks just as well, and a balloon wiped with a damp cloth stops sticking. Water carries the charge away.
A fridge magnet does not stick to the wall. Charge and magnetism are different things, with different rules.

explanation.en: Charge can be shifted a little inside an uncharged object. The balloon pulls the wall's opposite charge toward itself. Opposites are now nearest, so they attract.
